title: Brave Search API MCP Server: Setup Guide (2026)
summary: Brave Search API MCP server requires an API key to work. You'll know what tools are required and what costs to expect.
body_markdown:
## How the Brave Search MCP works


Strip it down and the Brave Search MCP server is a translation layer. It takes a tool call from your AI client, turns it into an HTTPS request to the Brave Search API, and hands the JSON back to the model.


That's nearly all it does, which is why it stays cheap to run.


### Client, server and API: the request path


Only the server box ever holds the API key.


*(illustration: AI client → Brave MCP server → Brave Search API)*


Compared with a raw API call, the server adds three things. It publishes tool schemas, so the model knows each tool's name, its arguments and their types before it calls anything.


It supports discovery, so any MCP client can list those tools without custom glue. And it lets several clients share one configured server instead of each carrying its own HTTP code and its own copy of the key.


Past those three, **it is all passthrough** . If a search returns something odd, the cause is almost always the query parameters or the Brave response, not a layer in between.


### Brave Search MCP stdio vs HTTP transport


With stdio, the client launches the server as a child process and talks to it over standard input and output. Nothing listens on a port, and the process dies with the client. That suits a single developer on one machine.


With HTTP, the server runs on its own and clients connect over the network, which suits a team sharing one instance.


The cost is that you now own a network service, so you need to think about who can reach it. MCP doesn't solve that for you.


### Where the API key is read


At startup the server reads the key from an environment variable, not from the model's prompt or tool arguments. In stdio mode, your client's config passes that variable to the child process. In HTTP mode, set it in the environment of the service itself.


Either way, a missing or wrong key doesn't fail at launch in a way you'll notice. It surfaces later as an auth error on the first search, so test one query right after setup.


Next comes choosing which of the server's tools to expose to the model.
